newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates fall on economic cheer.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates fall on economic cheer.

text.p: The bellwether one-month Cetes rate fell for the 10th straight week at Banco de Mexico's primary auction on Tuesday and investors remain cheered by recent good economic indicators out of Mexico, analysts said.

On Tuesday, the key 27-day rate fell 87 basis points to 18.59 percent at the auction, compared to an expected decline of 60 basis points that a Reuters survey of eight Cetes dealers found earlier in the day.
Last week, the government released numbers showing real gross domestic product grew 7.6 in the fourth quarter and 5.1 percent in 1996 over the year before.
Analysts said that the declining Cetes rates could give an additional impulse to the economic recovery.
Lower inflation has also helped drive down rates.
On Monday, Banco de Mexico said that the consumer price index rose 0.89 percent in the first half of February, well within expectations.
"Bids are continuing to be fed by optimism over the economy and above all by the numbers for growth and inflation," Banco Union economist Ricardo Vazquez said.
The peso has remained strong and interest rates have fallen on a flood of foreign funds into Mexico, analysts added.
"A strong inflow of funds has helped rates to fall," said Bancomer economist Carlos Rosales.
Analysts also pointed out that the yield curve is continuing to flatten out with investors moving out longer-term in the search for better yields.
That was clearly the case at the auction on Tuesday, because the decline of 87 basis points on one-month paper was matched with a decline of only 11 basis points on three-month paper.
The six-month paper fell 13 basis points to 22.47 percent.
However, the yield on the one-year paper rose, to yield 23.53 percent, compared to 23.40 percent last week.
Moreover, demand for the Cetes has been declining steadily.
On Tuesday, demand fell to 7.72 billion pesos, down from 8.95 billion last week, which itself was down 33 percent from the auction a week before, brokerage house Interacciones said in a report.
Analysts said this was a sign of increasing caution on the part of investors in the face of declining real interest rates.
In the secondary market on Tuesday, overnight Cetes rates closed down at 17.50 percent, the lowest rate since the 1994 peso devaluation.
